subject: Renewal amendment: EU residency + APAC pilot + cross-region failover
messages:
From: Claire Tan <claire.tan@medpointhealth.com>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.com>
Cc: Samuel Rhodes <sam.rhodes@medpointhealth.com>
Date: 2026-05-10T09:18:00Z
Subject: Renewal conversation: EU residency + APAC pilot + failover

Hi Soojin,

Thanks for the call yesterday. As we discussed, MedPoint's renewal is coming up at the end of June and we'd like to: (1) formalize EU data residency for all EU traffic, (2) pilot APAC burst capacity for our new Singapore customers with a warm-standby failover to EU, and (3) increase committed capacity from 200k tokens/day to 350k tokens/day during peak windows.

A few asks from our side to make legal and procurement move faster:
- A short amendment that captures the term extension (we're aiming for 24 months), committed capacity increase, and data residency guarantees.
- Pricing delta for the committed uplift and the APAC burst entitlement (expected 3 months pilot, then review).
- Confirmation of failover behavior (how traffic will route, FK caches or prefix behavior, and RTO targets).
- SOC 2 evidence and any residency attestation we can provide to our security team.

Can you send a mutual action plan (MAP) and a draft amendment we can review with procurement this week?

Appreciate it,
Claire
Cloud Ops, MedPoint Health
From: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.com>
To: Claire Tan <claire.tan@medpointhealth.com>
Cc: karthik.iyer@redwood.com, monica.patel@redwood.com
Date: 2026-05-11T14:02:00Z
Subject: Re: Renewal conversation: EU residency + APAC pilot + failover

Claire —

Thanks for the clear summary. I attached a draft amendment and a capacity calc for your review (see attachments). High level proposal below so procurement has something concrete tomorrow:

Proposal summary (high level)
- Term: 24 months starting 2026-07-01
- Committed capacity: increase to 350k tokens/day (monthly commit, carried over up to 20% unused to the next month)
- APAC Pilot: 3-month burst entitlement (up to additional 150k tokens/day peak available as warm-burst) included in month-to-month pricing for pilot window; pricing delta below
- Data residency: all EU-region customer traffic will be provisioned to EU nodes and logs retained in-region; cross-region failover allowed for continuity with additional protections (see technical note)
- Failover SLA: target RTO for full failover path is 60s for edge routing; warm-standby KV cache replication aims for <5s session warm-up (best-effort)

Pricing deltas (summary)
- Committed uplift: +12% on hosted per-token rate over current commitment (volume discount baked in)
- APAC pilot entitlement (3 mo): flat pilot fee of $18k total to reserve warm-burst capacity (credits applied if convert to committed capacity)

Next steps I recommend:
1) Karhik/Monica to confirm ops and any changes to SLO language.
2) We finalize amendment and route DocuSign for signatures.
3) Run a short test window (1 week) during pilot onboarding to validate cross-region routing and latency for a small subset of traffic.

I've cc'd Karhik and Monica to provide technical and ops details. If the summary looks aligned I can uplad to DocuSign and send a MAP with milestone dates for procurement.

Best,
Soojin Lee
Enterprise Account Executive, Redwood Inference
From: karthik.iyer@redwood.com <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.com>
Cc: monica.patel@redwood.com, lauren.bishop@redwood.com
Date: 2026-05-12T02:26:00Z
Subject: Re: Renewal conversation: EU residency + APAC pilot + failover

Folks —

Technical notes to include in amendment and runbook:
- EU residency: we will pin MedPoint EU traffic to dedicated EU node pool (eu-1) with in-region logging and KMS-backed key storage. This meets the majority of residency requirements we see.
- APAC pilot: implement as traffic split -> primary eu-1 with conditional warm-burst to apac-burst pool (sg-1). We will advertise warm-standby edges in APAC; traffic will only route there when EU capacity is saturated or per routing policy.
- KV cache replication: not full geo-replication — instead we snapshot prefix caches and pre-warm common session keys. Expect 2-5 seconds warm-up for conversational sessions depending on prompt size.
- Failover behavior: automated policy will route to sg-1 after 3 consecutive 500/timeout errors or when eu-1 drops below the configured capacity headroom threshold. Rollback window (automatic fallback) is 5 minutes after eu-1 health stabilized.
- Observability: we will surface token-level split, origin region, and failover events in the console and ship a summary web hook for your monitoring stack.

Ops ask from Security/Compliance: please have MedPoint share the minimum SOC2 report requirements and any EU data-at-rest certification language they need so we can scope the attestation. Our InfoSec can prep the residency attestation doc.

I linked the OPS ticket with the onboarding checklist and initial runbook template: https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/OPS-4982

-Karthik
Sr. Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference
From: Claire Tan <claire.tan@medpointhealth.com>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.com>
Cc: Samuel Rhodes <sam.rhodes@medpointhealth.com>, monica.patel@redwood.com
Date: 2026-05-12T17:03:00Z
Subject: Re: Renewal conversation: EU residency + APAC pilot + failover

Thanks — this looks promising. Procurement wants to confirm the following before we sign:
- Final per-token rate after the +12% uplift and exact monthly commitment billing cadence.
- That the APAC pilot fee is billable up front and refundable/creditable if we convert to committed APAC capacity.
- Exact language for SLOs around failover and data locality (we'll send redlines on the attestation).

Also, MedPoint would like to lock a 24-month term but start the APAC pilot in mid-August to coincide with their Singapore product launch. Is that timing reasonable?

We can jump on a 30-minute call Friday to align internal approvers if that helps.

-Claire
From: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.com>
To: Claire Tan <claire.tan@medpointhealth.com>
Cc: karthik.iyer@redwood.com, monica.patel@redwood.com, lauren.bishop@redwood.com
Date: 2026-05-13T16:42:00Z
Subject: Re: Renewal conversation: EU residency + APAC pilot + failover

Claire —

All good — we can accommodate the mid-August APAC pilot start and the 24-month term starting 2026-07-01. Quick answers and action items below:

Answers:
- Final rate: I'll send a redlined amendment with explicit per-token tiering and monthly invoice cadence; committed uplift is reflected as a blended rate in the attached draft.
- APAC pilot fee: billable up front; fully creditable against committed APAC capacity if you convert within 90 days of pilot close. We'll put that in the MAP.
- SLO language: Karhik will add the explicit failover thresholds and fallback windows; Security will provide a residency attestation template for procurement review.

Action items (owner / ETA)
- Soojin: finalize MAP and route DocuSign for amendment (ETA: 2026-05-14 EOD) — DocuSign link will be shared once legal signs off.
- Karhik: update runbook and SLO clause with exact thresholds (ETA: 2026-05-14) — OPS ticket OPS-4982.
- Monica: pull SOC2 artifact and residency attestation template for MedPoint security (ETA: 2026-05-15).
- Claire / MedPoint: confirm procurement approver list and available signature window (ETA: 2026-05-14)

If that timeline works, I'll push the amendment into DocuSign and include a short MAP with milestones: legal review, procurement review, signature, pilot kickoff planning. I'll also attach the draft amendment and the capacity spreadsheet for your procurement team.

Thanks — talk soon.
Soojin
Enterprise Account Executive, Redwood Inference
